newsitem.title: UK: Reuters swings to gains on revenue rise.
newsitem.headline: Reuters swings to gains on revenue rise.

text.p: Shares in Reuters reversed intraday losses and turned slightly higher on Friday after the international news and information organisation said revenue rose nine percent in the third quarter.
Reuters shares, which had traded around nine pence lower prior to the statement, were up five pence at 777-1/2p by 1127 GMT. Some 1.8 million shares had changed hands.
"We had been looking for revenues up between seven or nine percent so that was a good figure. Also, the statement on product sales and streamlining was quite encouraging," one marketmaker said.
Reuters said revenue rose nine percent to 736 million stg in the third quarter from a year earlier. Nine-month revenue was up 10 percent at 2.174 billion stg.

The company said sales of its new 3000 series products had met expectations so far. Chief executive Peter Job said heavy investment in the company's product line required the streamlining of its organisation.

"These figures were very much in line with expectations. There's nothing here that would suggest any change to forecasts or assessment of the stock," said Anthony de Larrinaga, media analyst at Panmure Gordon.
De Larrinaga said he had looked for a revenue rise of 9.6 percent to 742 million stg.
"The review of the 3000 series was slightly cautious, with talk about needing to maintain momentum. It's early days for the 3000 product but we like the look of it," he said.
De Larrinaga said he recommended holding the stock.
"It is reasonably up with events, and all these big media stocks are sensitive to moves on Wall Street. It's not overvalued," he said.
